display.title: The Hidden Broom Maker, Part 2
display.summary_short: Reb Leib Sarah's sends the leader of Kobrin to spend Shabbos with a poor broom maker deep in the forest, a hidden tzaddik whose prayers cancel the poritz's cruel decree.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with a story the Rebbe told for Parshas Vayeitzei: young Yisroel, later the Ruzhiner Rebbe, would ask Rashi's questions before seeing Rashi, but on Yaakov's dream of angels going up and down he asked nothing, explaining with a smile that in a dream strange things happen. Then the story continues. The new poritz of Kobrin demands years of back rent from the Jews and will cancel it only if they join his rebellion against the Russian Czar; Reb Leib Sarah's refuses, since Jews pray for the peace of their government. Instead he secretly sends Binyamin, the community leader, to spend Shabbos in the forest with Reb Yaakov, a poor broom maker who reads slowly from an old siddur. At night Binyamin hears heavenly zemiros and sees the hut blazing with light. After Havdalah Reb Yaakov announces that the decree is cancelled. Back in Kobrin, Binyamin learns that Russian soldiers arrested the poritz on Shabbos morning, and months later the governor reveals that the Czar has given the town's land to the Jews as a gift.
display.lesson: Hashem watches over His people through hidden tzaddikim, and Jews stay loyal and peaceful toward the government of the land.
